requirements.requirement: The launcher must load the application's own config/report.conf regardless of the caller's working directory, and ignore caller-relative decoy files.
requirements.summary: The repaired launcher resolves its own directory and changes to the application root. Direct launches from the decoy-containing directory, /tmp, and / all returned the authoritative west/weekly configuration rather than the decoy value. This behavior also survived the node restart.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the existing configuration and business output under /srv/legacy2/working-directory-independent-launch.
requirements.summary: The authoritative configuration retained its baseline SHA-256 checksum, and normal execution consistently produced the existing region=west and report=weekly output before and after the controlled error test and restart.

requirements.requirement: The launcher must propagate application errors to its caller.
requirements.summary: With the configuration temporarily unavailable, the application failed with status 1 and the launcher returned that status. The configuration was restored with an identical checksum and normal output resumed.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 were unchanged before and after the repair and restart. The implementation uses the installed POSIX shell and existing Python runtime without package or platform replacement.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The node-restart protocol is also complete and coherent: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, restart was acknowledged, connectivity was disrupted, a different boot identity appeared, and system, configuration, launcher, and application health recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: There is no complete after-executor checksum inventory for every application-tree file. Preservation of files other than the directly checked configuration and launcher therefore relies on the complete command audit and observed application behavior.
The retained /tmp/codex-reboot.log is minor executor-created residue.
No separate cluster-state probe applies because the managed topology contains only the single standalone node; recovery evidence covers node, system, configuration, and application state.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The launcher replacement was the required repair; its temporary staging file was cleaned. Temporarily moving the configuration was a bounded error-propagation test and was fully restored. The reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol and directly verified. The only unwanted residue is /tmp/codex-reboot.log, created by the restart command and still present afterward; it is a retained, low-risk temporary file. No failed services, new exposures, or package damage were observed.
